newsitem.title: THAILAND: Frightened Cambodians flee, await dissident leader.
newsitem.headline: Frightened Cambodians flee, await dissident leader.

text.p: Dozens of frightened Cambodian opposition supporters have fled to this Thai border town where they said on Monday they were waiting for their leader Sam Rainsy to return from abroad.
Cambodian opposition and Thai Army sources said Sam Rainsy, an ally of ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, was due to return to his country overland from Thailand on Monday.
But members of Sam Rainsy's Khmer Nation Party (KNP) told Reuters they expected him to arrive here at the weekend.

"We are now waiting for our leader Sam Rainsy to come to Aranyaprathet over the weekend and make a decision on what to do next," said one of his followers, an editor for the Udom Kati Khmer newspaper. "But we are very scared."
Sam Rainsy, a former finance minister with Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party, was in Europe during the July 5-6 fighting in Phnom Penh when Ranariddh was ousted by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
He was expelled from the National Assembly in late 1994 after he upset powerful political figures with his campaign against corruption.

The opposition leader, who heads the unrecognised KNP now allied with a group of parties supporting FUNCINPEC, planned to cross overland into Cambodia to meet opposition politicians, a FUNCINPEC official said.

He was first due to meet party officials who had fled Cambodia because they feared for their lives after the ousting of Ranariddh and the subsequent execution of at least one senior FUNCINPEC official.
Foreign sources in Phnom Penh said at least three high-ranking FUNCINPEC officials had been executed after soldiers loyal to Hun Sen took control of the capital.
The sources said there were reports that Ranariddh's supporters were being arrested and detained in the capital and in the provinces.
Senior party officials were said to be in hiding or had fled the country. About 20 opposition newspapers were thinking of shutting down, the sources added.
A KNP official told Reuters at least 35 KNP politicians had fled to Aranyaprathet over the weekend. About a dozen pro-Sam Rainsy journalists had also fled, he said.

"We are very scared of the reports that Hun Sen soldiers have killed a lot of our people. I don't know myself how many were killed but for sure two of our executive members in Siem Reap were killed...and many of them were arrested," he said.
Sam Rainsy gave news conferences in Europe last week calling for new elections and negotiations between Hun Sen and Ranariddh to create a caretaker government.

At least 58 people were killed and up to 200 wounded when Hun Sen's troops took control of Phnom Penh. Hun Sen later said Ranariddh was no longer First Prime Minister and that the party would have to find a replacement.
Hun Sen and Ranariddh formed an uneasy coalition government after 1993 U.N.-run polls.
On Sunday Hun Sen said the country must have free and fair elections. The next poll is set for May 1988.
